summary.goal:
Build a small library management system in this repository (Node.js, ES modules, no dependencies), with a command-line interface, persistence, validation, tests and documentation.

Storage: one JSON file, default `data/library.json` relative to the current directory; every command accepts `--data <path>` to use another file. Create the file on first use. Ids are integers assigned in order per entity type, starting at 1.

Modules (each with its own tests in test/ using node:test):
- src/books.js: addBook({ title, author, copies = 1 }), listBooks({ available } = {}); a book is { id, title, author, copies, available }.
- src/members.js: addMember({ name }); a member is { id, name }.
- src/loans.js: checkout({ bookId, memberId, days = 14, today }), returnLoan({ loanId, today }), listLoans({ memberId, overdue, today } = {}), report({ today }). A loan is { id, bookId, memberId, out, due, returned: null | date, fine }. Dates are strings YYYY-MM-DD; `today` defaults to the current date. Rules: checkout fails when the book has no available copy or the member already has 3 active loans; returning a loan after its due date charges a fine of 0.50 per day late, capped at 20.00; returning a loan twice fails.

CLI: bin/library.js, run as `node bin/library.js <command> [options] [--data <path>]`. Every successful command prints one JSON value on stdout and exits 0. Every failure prints `{ "error": "<message>" }` on stderr and exits 2 (unknown command or missing option: exit 1).
- `add-book --title <t> --author <a> [--copies <n>]` prints the book.
- `add-member --name <n>` prints the member.
- `checkout --book <id> --member <id> [--days <n>] [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints the loan.
- `return --loan <id> [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints the loan with its fine.
- `list-books [--available]` prints an array of books.
- `list-loans [--member <id>] [--overdue] [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints an array of loans (`--overdue` keeps only active loans whose due date is before today).
- `report [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints { books, copies, available, members, activeLoans, overdue, finesOwed } where finesOwed is the sum of the fines of every returned loan.

Add a "test" script to package.json so that `npm test` runs every test, and write a README.md that documents the modules, every command with an example, and the rules. npm test must pass.

tasks.spec:
Build the shared foundation every other task depends on; the API is frozen in the design doc §4.2 and must be implemented verbatim, because books/members/loans are written against it in parallel.

1. src/errors.js: export `class LibraryError extends Error` with `this.name = 'LibraryError'`.
2. src/store.js: export DEFAULT_DATA_PATH ('data/library.json'), setDataPath(path), getDataPath(), emptyStore(), readStore(path = getDataPath()), writeStore(path, data), nextId(items). Behaviour: getDataPath returns an absolute path resolved against process.cwd() at call time, and falls back to DEFAULT_DATA_PATH when setDataPath received null/undefined; readStore creates the file and any missing parent directories containing emptyStore() when the file is absent, tolerates a parsed object that omits books/members/loans (missing collections become []), and throws LibraryError('invalid data file: <path>') when the file is not valid JSON or its top level is not an object; writeStore writes `<path>.tmp` and renames it over `<path>`, serialising with JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) plus a trailing newline; nextId returns max(id)+1 over the array, or 1 when empty. No dependencies, no node:fs usage outside this file.

The suite must be runnable with `npm test` from the project root and must not create anything inside the repository's own data/ directory.

Implement src/books.js exactly as designed in the design doc §6.1, using readStore/writeStore/nextId from src/store.js and LibraryError from src/errors.js (never import node:fs).

- addBook({ title, author, copies = 1 }): trim title and author; reject a missing/empty title or author with LibraryError('title is required' / 'author is required'); reject copies that is not an integer >= 1 ('copies must be a positive integer'); assign id = nextId(data.books), set available = copies, append to data.books, save, and return the stored book object { id, title, author, copies, available }.
- listBooks({ available } = {}): return the books in ascending id order; when `available` is truthy return only books whose available > 0.

tasks.spec:
Implement src/loans.js per the design doc §6.3, using readStore/writeStore/nextId from src/store.js and LibraryError from src/errors.js. Import nothing from books.js or members.js: read and write data.books and data.members directly through the store, which keeps this task independent of them.

Exports: checkout, returnLoan, listLoans, report, plus the date helpers todayISO(), addDays(iso, n), diffDays(fromIso, toIso).

- checkout({ bookId, memberId, days = 14, today }): ids must be integers, days an integer >= 1, today a YYYY-MM-DD string naming a real date (default todayISO(), local time); the book and the member must exist; book.available must be >= 1; the member must have fewer than 3 loans with returned === null. Creates { id: nextId(loans), bookId, memberId, out: today, due: addDays(today, days), returned: null, fine: 0 }, decrements book.available, saves and returns the loan. Nothing outside this function may decrement available.
- returnLoan({ loanId, today }): the loan must exist and have returned === null, otherwise LibraryError. Sets returned = today, fine = Math.round(Math.min(20, 0.5 * Math.max(0, diffDays(due, today))) * 100) / 100, increments the book's available (cap it at copies), saves and returns the loan. On-time or early returns get fine 0.
- listLoans({ memberId, overdue, today } = {}): all loans in ascending id order, filtered by memberId when given; `overdue` truthy keeps only loans with returned === null && due < today (ISO strings compare correctly); filters combine with AND.
- report({ today }): { books, copies, available, members, activeLoans, overdue, finesOwed } as described in the design doc, with finesOwed the cents-rounded sum of the fine of every returned loan.

resolveToday() only validates an explicitly supplied `today`; an absent or undefined key falls back to todayISO(), so both report() and report({ today: undefined }) (how the CLI calls it) default to the current date.

tasks.title: bin/library.js: checkout, return, list-loans and report
tasks.spec:
Extend the CLI built by `cli-base` with the remaining four commands, using its command table and its exit-code rules (design doc §7) rather than adding a second code path:
- checkout --book <id> --member <id> [--days <n>] [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>] -> checkout({ bookId, memberId, days, today }) and print the loan.
- return --loan <id> [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>] -> returnLoan({ loanId, today }) and print the loan with its fine.
- list-loans [--member <id>] [--overdue] [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>] -> listLoans({ memberId, overdue, today }) and print the array; --member maps to memberId, --overdue to true.
- report [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>] -> report({ today }) and print the object.
Optional options that are absent must be left undefined so the module defaults apply. Errors keep the same shape and exit codes as before (1 for usage problems, 2 for thrown errors).

Extend test/cli.test.js (keep the existing cases passing) with a full terminal scenario driven only through the CLI against one temp --data file: add-book with two copies, add-member, checkout, list-loans showing the active loan, --overdue on a due date still in the future printing [], return with a --today 20 days after the due date printing fine 10.00, a second return exiting 2, list-books showing available back at 2, and report printing books/copies/available/members/activeLoans/overdue/finesOwed with the expected numbers. Also cover checkout with too few arguments exiting 1 and checkout for an unknown book exiting 2 with stderr JSON and empty stdout.

Implementation: bin/library.js now imports { checkout, listLoans, report, returnLoan } from ../src/loans.js and adds four entries to the existing `commands` table, reusing the shared parser/validator/coercer/output path and exit-code logic — no second code path. Each run() builds the module argument object from the parsed values, so absent optional options stay `undefined` and module defaults apply (`--days` -> 14, `--today` -> todayISO()). `list-loans` declares optional ['member','today'], flags ['overdue'], numbers ['member'], and maps `--member` to `memberId` and `--overdue` to true inside run(); because `flags` is the union across entries, `--overdue` is automatically valueless with no parser change. `checkout` marks book/member/days as numbers so they go through Number() and the loans module validates integer-ness (--book abc -> exit 2), while missing required options (too few arguments) -> exit 1.

checkout/return/list-loans declare their id options in `numbers` so Number() coercion happens centrally and the loans module surfaces bad values (--book abc) as validation failures with exit 2.
In list-loans the CLI option is `--member` but the module field is `memberId`; the mapping happens in the run() closure, consistent with the other commands' shape differences (e.g. --book -> bookId).

projectEvents.note: cli-base (bin/library.js): the parser is table-driven — `commands` maps name -> { required: string[], optional: string[], flags: string[], numbers: string[], run(values) }. To add a command (cli-loans), add one entry; parse/validate/coerce/output are shared. Key details cli-loans must match: (1) option names are the long name without dashes (e.g. --book -> required:['book'], numbers:['book']); `numbers` entries are passed through Number() before run(), everything else stays a string. (2) Valueless flags are derived automatically from the union of every entry's `flags`, so adding e.g. flags:['overdue'] to list-loans makes --overdue valueless with no parser change. (3) `--data` is extracted during parsing into a separate dataPath and applied via setDataPath before run(), so it is accepted before or after the command name and is legal for every command. (4) Exit 1 cases: missing command, unknown command, unknown option for the command, a valued option with no following non-option token, and an unexpected extra positional argument. Exit 2: anything thrown by run() (LibraryError or unexpected), message written as {"error":...} to stderr. Success writes JSON.stringify(value)+"\n" to stdout and exits 0.
